paper.title: Thompson Sampling: An Asymptotically Optimal Finite Time Analysis

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic multi-armed bandit with Bernoulli rewards
settings.definition_quote: Associated with each action, $a$, is an unknown Bernoulli distribution $\cB\left(\mu_a\right)$, whose expectation is $\mu_a$. At each time $t$ the agent chooses to observe an action $A_t\in\{1,\dots,K\}$ and receives a reward $R_t$ drawn from the distribution $\cB\left(\mu_{A_t}\right)$. ... For the rest of this paper, we assume action $1$ is the unique optimal action.

symbols.C_const: problem-dependent constant C(epsilon, mu_1, ..., mu_K), independent of T

source.quote: For every $\epsilon>0$ there exists a problem-dependent constant $C(\epsilon,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K)$ such that the regret of Thompson Sampling satisfies: \[ \cR(T)\leq(1+\epsilon)\sum_{a\in A:\mu_a\neq\mu^*}\frac{\Delta_a(\ln(T)+\ln\ln(T))}{K(\mu_a,\mu^*)}+ C(\epsilon,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K). \]

results.notes: Regret defined as sum of gaps times expected pulls, i.e. pseudo-regret. TS does not use T, so anytime. K(.,.) is Bernoulli KL, mapped to kl_i.

bound.regime: for every eps>0, every suboptimal arm a

symbols.C_b: constant from Proposition 1 bounding sum_t P(N_{1,t} <= t^b)

source.label: Thm2Arm
source.quote: Let $\epsilon>0$. With $b$ as in Proposition \ref{important:lemma}, for every suboptimal arm $a$, there exist constants $D(\epsilon,\mu_1,\mu_a)$, $N(b,\epsilon,\mu_1,\mu_a)$ and $N_0(b)$ such that: \bE[N_{a,T}] \leq (1+\epsilon)\frac{\ln(T) + \ln\ln (T) }{K(\mu_a,\mu_1)} + D(\epsilon,\mu_1,\mu_a) + N(b,\epsilon,\mu_1,\mu_a)+N_0(b) + 5 + 2C_b .

results.notes: Bound on the expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm a (quantity 'other'); kl_i refers to K(mu_a, mu_1). Proof uses T>=e.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic Bernoulli K-armed bandit, strongly consistent policies; lower bound on expected number of pulls of each suboptimal arm

bound.regime: T -> infinity; bound on E[N_{a,T}]/ln T
